WHO.title: Who decides for Memphis?
WHO.question: Nine decisions that shape a Memphis family's week. Who made each one: the city, the state in Nashville, or Washington?

decisions.q: The lowest wage a Memphis employer may pay
decisions.detail: Tennessee has no state minimum wage, so the federal $7.25 applies, and a 2013 state law bars cities and counties from requiring private employers to pay more.

decisions.q: Whether Memphis workers get paid sick leave
decisions.detail: The same 2013 law bars local governments from requiring leave policies beyond state and federal law.
decisions.src: HR Daily Advisor, on Tennessee's 2013 law

decisions.detail: In May 2026 the legislature split the 9th District, the state's only majority-Black district, into three, and the governor signed the map the same day. The NAACP sued in state court.

decisions.q: Who controls the budget and the superintendent of Memphis-Shelby County Schools
decisions.detail: A 2026 state law created a nine-member board appointed by the governor and the two legislative speakers, with final say over the budget, large contracts and the superintendent until 2030. The district and the county commission sued.

decisions.q: Whether federal agents and the National Guard patrol Memphis streets
decisions.detail: A presidential memorandum created the Memphis Safe Task Force, which began on September 29, 2025, with the governor's support for the Guard.

decisions.q: Whether the Justice Department's findings on Memphis police still stand
decisions.detail: The department found a pattern of excessive force and discrimination in December 2024, then closed the case and retracted the findings in May 2025.

decisions.q: Whether Memphis would negotiate a federal consent decree on policing in 2024
decisions.detail: The city told the Justice Department it would not enter an agreement in principle; the police chief pointed to changes already made.

decisions.q: When someone with a felony record can vote again
decisions.detail: A 2026 state law dropped the rule that all court costs be paid first and eased the child-support rule; Tennessee still has more than 400,000 people who cannot vote because of a felony.

decisions.q: Whether a low-wage Memphis parent can get Medicaid
decisions.detail: Tennessee has not expanded Medicaid; TennCare covers a parent only up to 100% of the poverty level.

WHO.notice: Count where each decision was made. Then run it in Denver, where the city sets its own wage. The frustration is not only what was decided, but how little of it was decided in Memphis.
WHO.yourCall: Pick one decision made in Nashville. Who would have to agree for Memphis to decide it for itself, and what would they say?

decisions.q: The lowest wage a Denver employer may pay
decisions.detail: Denver sets its own minimum wage, $19.29 an hour in 2026, after Colorado let cities do so in 2019.

decisions.q: Whether Denver workers get paid family and medical leave
decisions.detail: Colorado voters approved FAMLI in 2020; it pays up to 12 weeks. A separate 2020 state law gives paid sick leave at employers of every size.
decisions.src: Denver shared mirror (FAMLI; Healthy Families and Workplaces Act)

decisions.detail: An independent 12-member commission, created when voters passed Amendment Y in 2018, took the job from the legislature.

decisions.q: Whether Denver police use license-plate cameras
decisions.detail: The city council rejected a Flock contract extension unanimously in May 2025, the mayor extended it with new limits, and in 2026 the council approved 50 Axon cameras, 7 to 6.

decisions.q: How Coloradans vote, and whether people on parole may vote
decisions.detail: Colorado mails every registered voter a ballot, registers voters automatically, and since 2019 lets people on parole vote.
decisions.src: Colorado Secretary of State; Colorado Springs Gazette

decisions.q: Whether a low-wage Denver parent can get Medicaid
decisions.detail: Colorado expanded Medicaid under the Affordable Care Act: adults qualify up to about 133% of the poverty level.
decisions.src: Denver shared mirror (Health First Colorado, HCPF)

decisions.q: Whether those Medicaid adults must report work hours from 2027
decisions.detail: The 2025 federal budget law adds work or community-engagement requirements for expansion adults from January 1, 2027, in every expansion state.
